questions.question_text: State the radius of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=64$.

options.why: Read the radius straight off the right side without taking the square root.
Halved the right side instead of taking its square root.
Took a square root of a square root, using the fourth root of $64$.

questions.question_text: State the radius of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=8$, in simplest surd form.

options.why: Correct value but not simplified — $\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}$.
Took out $4$ instead of $2$ when simplifying the surd.
Halved the right side instead of taking its square root.

questions.question_text: Write the equation of the circle centred at the origin with radius $9$.

options.why: Used the radius directly instead of squaring it.
Doubled the radius instead of squaring it.
Took the square root of the radius instead of squaring it.
Used the right side $4$ as the radius instead of $\sqrt{4}=2$.
Gave the $y$-intercepts instead of the $x$-intercepts.
Square-rooted the radius $2$ again instead of using it directly.

questions.solution_text:
$x^{2}+y^{2}=4$
$r=\sqrt{4}=2$
The circle crosses the $x$-axis at $(\pm r,0)$.
$x$-intercepts: $(2,0)$ and $(-2,0)$

questions.question_text: Which of the following points lies on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=100$?

options.why: $6^{2}+4^{2}=52$, which does not equal $100$.
Used both coordinates as the radius; $10^{2}+10^{2}=200$.
Split $100$ into two equal coordinates instead of testing $x^{2}+y^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
$6^{2}+8^{2}$
$=36+64$
$=100$
The coordinates satisfy $x^{2}+y^{2}=100$, so $(6,8)$ lies on the circle.

options.why: Used the radius $7$ directly instead of squaring it.
Used the diameter $14$ instead of $r^{2}$.
Squared the diameter $14$ instead of the radius.

questions.question_text: A circle is centred at the origin and passes through the point $(7,24)$. Find its equation.

options.why: Stopped at the radius $r=25$ instead of using $r^{2}$.
Added the coordinates $7+24$ instead of $7^{2}+24^{2}$.
Doubled $r^{2}$, as if the radius were the diameter.

questions.question_text: The point $(k,6)$ lies on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=100$. Find the possible values of $k$.

options.why: Gave only the positive root; $k^{2}=64$ has two solutions.
Left the answer as $k^{2}=64$ without taking the square root.
Subtracted $6$ instead of $6^{2}$ from $100$.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the point $(6,2)$ lies inside, on, or outside the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=36$.

options.why: Used only $6^{2}=36$ and ignored the $y$-coordinate of $2$.
Added the coordinates as $6+2=8$, which is less than $36$.

questions.solution_text:
$6^{2}+2^{2}$
$=36+4$
$=40$
Since $40>36$, the point lies outside the circle.

questions.question_text: Show that the points $P(1,7)$ and $Q(7,1)$ both lie on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=50$, and hence state the radius in simplest surd form.

options.why: Gave $r^{2}=50$ instead of the radius $\sqrt{50}$.
Correct length but not simplified — $\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$.
Took out $25$ instead of $5$ when simplifying $\sqrt{50}$.

questions.solution_text:
$1^{2}+7^{2}=1+49=50$
$7^{2}+1^{2}=49+1=50$
Both points satisfy $x^{2}+y^{2}=50$, so both lie on the circle.
$r=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$
